subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin felt moved by Glabbagool's stillness and believed it signaled that Glabbagool had done something worth doing.
source_quote: I thought: that's the face of someone who did a thing worth doing.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin considered Glabbagool’s lack of fixed appendages made him tactically unpredictable and potentially dangerous.
source_quote: But he's unpredictable, because there are no fixed appendages.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin thought that Glabbagool being equipped as a weapon was wrong because weapons don’t have agency.
source_quote: It's not a weapon. Weapons don't have agency.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believed Dawnbringer had agency, and acknowledged that he himself was also annoying.
source_quote: Weapons don't have agency. Except mine. I'm annoying also, Dawnbringer.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin knew Eldeth’s departure was coming and had accepted it intellectually before she spoke.
source_quote: I'd known it was coming.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin felt he didn’t fit in dwarven society because he was too giant-raised for dwarven spaces and too dwarven for the hills.
source_quote: I had spent most of my life not being the right kind of dwarf for any given room. Too giant-raised for dwarven spaces, too dwarven for the hills.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wanted to petition to become part of Eldeth’s clan and asked if there was a hazing ritual.
source_quote: Is there any way that I can petition to become part of your clan? A pledge, perhaps? Is there a hazing ritual involved?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin felt a sense of relief and rightness when Eldeth swore she would bring him into her clan after reporting to the lords.
source_quote: Something settled in me at that. The kind of settling that happens when a thing you've been carrying turns out to have been lighter than you thought, or heavier, or just — right.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wanted to learn about his dwarven roots and become an integrated person who honored both his giant upbringing and his cultural heritage.
source_quote: I do want to learn about my dwarven roots. I want to become an integrated person — both my giant upbringing, but also my cultural roots, so, you know.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believed Eldeth’s promise was sincere and not just social nicety.
source_quote: I don't think you're just being socially nice here. I think you really do want me to.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin resented that he had chosen Tremor Sense for underground travel, and now that they were above ground, it was useless.
source_quote: I picked it because we were gonna be fucking underground all the time... And then the one time I need it. We're not underground, and we're not surrounded by fucking stone.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir still scanned his surroundings compulsively after emerging from the Underdark, because his habits hadn't adjusted to open space.
source_quote: The third day of open sky and I still hadn't stopped scanning.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir found the surface world disorienting because it was too loud with information he couldn’t properly interpret.
source_quote: I had too much information and not enough of the right kind. It was disorienting in a way I didn't have language for.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed the northern treeline was wrong because of unnatural stillness — no birds, no wind movement in undergrowth.
source_quote: The trees north of us were wrong. Not visibly wrong. The wrongness was in the negative space — the way no birds had moved through that section for some time, the way the undergrowth hadn't shifted with the wind in quite the pattern it should.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realized the thing following them was not a deer, despite Grygum’s conclusion.
source_quote: The three of us looked at each other in the way that the Ember Vanguard has developed as a private language: no words, just a shared acknowledgment that the thing in the trees is not a deer.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recognized the follower was patient and skilled, pacing them rather than trailing, indicating deliberate intent.
source_quote: Whatever was in those trees had been moving with us, shifting position laterally to stay in the blind spots, using the terrain the way someone uses it when they know what they're doing. Not panicked. Not rushing. Patient. The kind of following that isn't trailing — it's pacing.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir understood dusk was the worst possible time for the follower to strike — too dark for detail, too bright for shadow work.
source_quote: Dusk came in from the west... which meant we'd reached the worst possible window: too dark for fine detail, too bright for shadow work.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalled that goblin equality and inclusion on the surface was currently poor.
source_quote: The state of goblin equality and inclusion is rough at the moment.

subject: Spiderbait
fact: Spiderbait believed goblins were fully integrated into surface society and that he could safely explore alone.
source_quote: I'm just gonna go explore. It's totally safe for goblins, right? Nobody's gonna attack a goblin for being a goblin. We're totally integrated into the society.

subject: Spiderbait
fact: Spiderbait decided to follow Thorin and the group because he felt safer with them than alone.
source_quote: Do you mind if I just sort of hang out with you guys? Maybe find a nice place?

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool was witnessing the sun with a stillness that was not his usual passive state.
source_quote: Glabbagool just looked up... and there was something in the stillness of him that wasn't his usual stillness. He wasn't being a floor. He was witnessing.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer radiated warmth like a hearth, not directed at any one person but present for all.
source_quote: It radiated warmth the way a hearth does — not directed at anything in particular, just present.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noticed Dawnbringer warmed slightly when he said they understood each other.
source_quote: The hilt warmed slightly.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realized he had forgotten how to interpret environmental silence after months underground.
source_quote: I remember thinking I could be training instead. I don't remember what he said.

subject: Eldeth's promise
fact: Eldeth swore she would make it a statement of purpose that Thorin be embraced by her clan after reporting to the lords.
source_quote: I swear.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes his frustration about the stone and terrain mismatch is legitimate because he prepared reasonably for a different environment.
source_quote: He wasn't wrong about the stone. And his frustration was legitimate — he'd made a reasonable preparation for a reasonable environment, and we'd somehow ended up standing in the one terrain where it didn't apply.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir considered Thorin’s suggestion to fireball the trees but deemed it unworthy of serious thought.
source_quote: I considered this briefly, which is about as much time as it deserves.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz had already decided to get intel out of the situation before announcing his plan to misty step into the tree.
source_quote: I want to get some intel out of this," he said, the way a man says a thing when he's already decided what he's going to do.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir did not rule out the possibility that the tracker might be Jimjar coming to drag them back underground.
source_quote: I did not rule it out.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed Daz’s bird call worked and was pleased it had succeeded.
source_quote: I thought: *good. That actually worked.*

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum was proud of his own terrible imitation of a bird call.
source_quote: He was very proud of it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum earnestly wondered whether birds are a kind of ooze.
source_quote: Is it a kind of ooze?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum struggled to understand the concept of birds being feathered, as it conflicted with his existing mental framework.
source_quote: I watched the concept try to find somewhere to settle and fail to locate purchase.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes the divine plan has them covered, even if provisionally and subject to revision by evidence.
source_quote: The divine plan has us covered, in the broadest possible sense — or at least I choose to believe it does, provisionally, and correct the belief when the evidence demands it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed movement from the north and interpreted it as a skilled follower, not a random threat.
source_quote: Thorin had picked up something in the terrain earlier — movement from the north, not panicked, not aggressive, careful.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed the drow spy was not a predator but a professional doing a job she’d rather not be doing.
source_quote: That combination doesn't say assassin to me. It says someone who got handed a bad assignment and is making the best of it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thought the drow spy had been given an assignment that would earn her a sincere complaint if she returned home.
source_quote: Whoever sent a drow to the surface in daylight to shadow a party through open forest had, I thought, given that drow exactly the kind of assignment that earns you a very sincere complaint when you get back home.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum was observing the drow spy’s face to read her emotional state, even while she was still stunned.
source_quote: I stood back and let him work, watching the spy's face for what it told me — not yet, she was still too stunned, still in that soft-edged blankness...

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed the drow spy’s bravery during her approach was a performance masking inner desperation.
source_quote: She'd put on a brave face for the whole approach.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the drow spy was not watching the party but was intensely trying not to look at him.
source_quote: She wasn't watching the party. She was watching me. And working very, very hard to make it look like she wasn't.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recognized the drow spy’s behavior as a learned social skill from Menzoberranzan — avoiding direct gaze at what one is most interested in.
source_quote: The particular discipline of *not looking at the thing you are most interested in* is one of the first social skills anyone learns in the city.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized the drow spy was following him specifically because he was being used as bait to draw out the person who paid for his protection.
source_quote: So basically, you're treating me as bait. You're watching and observing so that when something happens to me, you can go report back what happened to me.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz understood that House T'sarran’s matron mother was waiting for the person who paid for his protection to reveal themselves on the surface.
source_quote: We are looking for that person, not for you.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recalled a lesson from his training in Menzoberranzan: know who holds the debt before deciding whether to collect it.
source_quote: I thought of something a training instructor had said once... *The first rule of the House: know who holds the debt before you decide whether to collect it.*

subject: Daz
fact: Daz felt the drow spy’s revelation about being used as bait was a moment of personal revelation, connecting his past to his present danger.
source_quote: The full picture came out under continued pressure... I turned it over once. Twice.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed a fracture in the drow spy’s composure when he offered her a new job.
source_quote: Something shifted in her face. A tiny, involuntary fracture in the composure. *Wait. I might live?*

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed the prayer beads broke through the drow spy’s professional armor because they represented an unknown, alien threat.
source_quote: Unknown religious ritual from an alien faith, administered by a half-orc? That slipped right past every prepared defense.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum perceived the drow spy as defeated, frustrated, and annoyed after the beads were given and persuasion succeeded.
source_quote: She looked, in the GM's precise summary, defeated, frustrated, annoyed.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believed telling the drow spy to report her failure to her matron would be a fate worse than death.
source_quote: He walked up and told her we could simply let her go — report her failure to her matron, "let them know how pathetic you are."

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin laughed at the drow spy’s response to his intimidation, but recognized she was still engaging with them.
source_quote: She laughed in his face... She was laughing, but she was also still talking to us...

subject: Daz
fact: Daz felt no superiority over Thorin’s failed intimidation tactics, recognizing Thorin’s physical honesty as valuable despite his lack of drow political skill.
source_quote: I didn't feel superior about this. Thorin's instincts have saved us too many times for me to feel superior.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz admitted he sounded absurd when he said he’d been underground for a while, realizing how alien it sounded to a drow.
source_quote: I'm drow, but I've been underground for a while.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz corrected himself after realizing his statement sounded absurd, acknowledging he’d been away from home for a while.
source_quote: Let me correct that. I've been away from home for a while.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz understood that the drow spy’s contemptuous look toward him was rooted in disbelief that he could be so out of touch with drow society.
source_quote: She stared at me... "You realize how absurd that sounds?"

subject: Daz
fact: Daz interpreted the drow spy’s final admission — that she was following him to find the person who paid for his protection — as confirmation of his own significance in a larger, hidden conflict.
source_quote: We are looking for that person, not for you.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz understands that he is being used as an indicator or bait to reveal who is protecting him.
source_quote: I understood what had just been said about me. Not Daz. Not even the wizard. The *indicator.* The piece on the board that you move to see who else moves in response. The bait.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz decided he would give himself until they reached Candlekeep to develop the appropriate perspective on being used as bait.
source_quote: I thought about it for a moment and decided I'd give myself until we reached Candlekeep to develop the appropriate perspective.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz knows he is the only person in the party who treats information as a finite and valuable resource.
source_quote: I am categorically on record as being the only person in this party who treats information as a finite and valuable resource

subject: Daz
fact: Daz felt that being the subject of theoretical murder planning while a restrained enemy watched was fine, because he had found purpose.
source_quote: I kept my expression neutral. I have found purpose. I am the feared mage of the Ember Vanguard. This is fine.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir filed away Thorin’s comment about nicknaming the drow 'Polly Pocket' as demeaning.
source_quote: Nickname her Polly Pocket," he said. Then, with the flat authority of someone who knows what he's doing: "It's very demeaning." I filed that away.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed Glabbagool’s steady, unblinking attention to the miniaturized drow spy as the most earnest thing he’d seen in weeks.
source_quote: I noticed — not the spy's indignation, not Thorin's satisfaction, but Glabbagool, walking with one eye locked permanently on the prisoner. He had been assigned a job. He was doing the job. The care in it — the steadiness of that unblinking attention — was the most earnest thing I'd seen in weeks.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realized he should have thought about what it would be like for Glabbagool to be confined in a bag with a furious, miniaturized assassin as his only company.
source_quote: I'd told him I'd protect him from corrupting forces. I hadn't thought about what it would be like to be carried in a bag with a furious, newly miniaturized assassin as your only company. I should have thought about that.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir understood that the drow woman’s confinement — small, surveilled, breathing through holes, shielded from sunlight — was the most honest description of their mercy.
source_quote: She was small, surveilled by an ooze, breathing through holes we'd poked in the bag, and being shielded from sunlight as a kindness. The most honest description of our mercy I could have asked for.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thought about Asha Vandree and how she would have hated that her theological document would unlock questions in Candlekeep’s library.
source_quote: I thought about Asha Vandree, briefly. The way she had looked through me the entire time we were in that room... She would have hated that.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir was curious what Glabbagool would ask as his one question at Candlekeep, though he did not say so aloud.
source_quote: I was also curious what he'd ask. I didn't say so, but I thought about it for the better part of the road to Candlekeep

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed that Glabbagool was watching the bag of holding with one eye, and kept watching it.
source_quote: I kept watching the bag, the way it moved, the slight weight of it. Somewhere in there, one eye was open.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum spent the road to Candlekeep turning over the same questions in his head about what Bahamut truly wants from him personally.
source_quote: I'd spent most of it turning the same questions over in my head like stones I kept expecting to find something under. What does Bahamut actually want from me? Not the general want... but the specific want. The personal assignment.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum felt he should have brought a better book to Candlekeep.
source_quote: I felt like I should have brought a better book.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum agreed with Thorin that therapy is a process, not a product.
source_quote: He nodded gravely. We understood each other.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum assigned Glabbagool to keep the miniaturized drow spy under control.
source_quote: I assigned Glabbagool to keep her under control, which felt like the appropriate use of available resources. "We'll have a goal," I said. "Keep her under control."

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is skeptical of the drow spy’s proposed deal because it has no enforcement mechanism and dissolves when her interests diverge from theirs.
source_quote: I don't buy it. The minute she has the information she needs, she's off, and we get jack shit.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes that killing Daz temporarily and reviving him could reveal who is protecting him.
source_quote: Do it, but make sure we can bring them back.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin thinks the drow spy’s confidence in escaping Candlekeep means they shouldn’t take her into the stronghold.
source_quote: She's so confident she can escape, I don't think we want to be taking her into the stronghold.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin intentionally spoke loudly about the prayer beads being more potent to make the drow spy reconsider her options.
source_quote: Those prayer beads are at full power, even though they're shrunken, right?" ... "More potent. Okay. Good to know.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes the drow spy’s confinement in the bag of holding — with holes for air and shade from the sun — is mercy.
source_quote: This is mercy," Thorin confirmed.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin thinks therapy is not a one-question thing and requires a process.
source_quote: Okay, but I mean, like, I'm looking for a therapist. This is not a one-question type of thing. This is — there are no shortcuts when it comes to therapy.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin proposed giving Glabbagool his own question at Candlekeep because he thought it was fair.
source_quote: Thorin, ever practical, pointed out that we were the primary sources — she could just interview us and save herself the reading. Then he proposed giving Glabbagool his own question, which I thought was extremely fair.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is confused by the concept of a library with limited questions and doesn’t understand why they don’t donate all books to ask unlimited questions.
source_quote: He wanted to know why we weren't simply donating every book we'd ever seen and asking questions until the end of time.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool explained that his googly eyes are just affectations and that he can see in other ways, but uses them because people take him more kindly.
source_quote: I can actually see different ways. This is how ooze work. But I discovered that if you have these cute eyes, people take you more friendly.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recognized that the drow spy’s claim about escaping Candlekeep implies she knows how to escape the prison.
source_quote: So they know how to escape that prison," I observed. "Is what they're telling us.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir understood that the Underdark’s coldness is structural, not personal, and that Asha Vandree’s erasure was the same.
source_quote: I had been furniture; I had noticed the quality of her erasure without taking it personally, because it wasn't personal — it was structural, the way the Underdark is cold. You don't take the cold personally.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum mentally filed Thorin's response under 'correct.'
source_quote: I mentally filed that under "correct."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum tried to look modest about being singled out by the First Reader and mostly failed.
source_quote: I tried to look modest about this and mostly failed.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum felt in demand when Vareth reacted to him with intense recognition.
source_quote: I'm feeling, I said, to no one in particular, "in demand here."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum knew the story of Stroud beating Protanther at chess because it had once comforted him.
source_quote: I know this story. I know it the way you know a story that someone told you when you were young and uncertain, when you needed proof that the impossible was occasionally available as an option.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum found the story of Stroud's chess win deeply comforting because it showed that preparation can still have blind spots.
source_quote: Four hundred years of preparation still has a blind spot.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum tested Vareth’s sincerity by stating the traditional expectation for Bahamut clerics.
source_quote: You have to understand, I said, with the measured cadence I use when I'm testing someone, "that it is traditional for clerics of Bahamut to want to try to take over the world. But I haven't moved into that phase yet."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum finished Vareth’s thought by saying, "It truly was legendary."
source_quote: I felt it coming together and finished the thought for him: "It truly was legendary."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum coined the term "Stroud's Gambit" because it had been sitting in the back of his mind since the journey began.
source_quote: And then, because I couldn't help it, and because the phrase had been sitting in the back of my mind since we started this journey and I'd never had the right audience for it: "Stroud's Gambit."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum claimed that his conversion and behavior were all part of a plan.
source_quote: Oh," I said, as warmly as I could manage, "it's all part of the plan."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum confirmed that Daz's habit of citing Malfire had become an ambient condition for the party.
source_quote: Yeah," I said, when someone turned to me for confirmation, "it's like we're kind of sick of each other, but somehow still together, yeah."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum quoted Malfire in Volume 3 to end the conversation about Daz's citations.
source_quote: As Malfire said in Volume 3.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum took notes because it's what he does.
source_quote: I took notes. It's what I do.

subject: Grygum's theological questions
fact: Grygum has unanswered questions about Bahamut's intentions and the meaning of his conversion, which remain unresolved.
source_quote: I didn't know what I was going to find. I had notes — the prayer book, the theological documents, the accumulated evidence of months in the Underdark — and I had questions...

subject: Grygum's journey
fact: Grygum carries the comfort of believing that sometimes the person who doesn't know what they're doing walks into the right room and everything clicks.
source_quote: I had the particular comfort of knowing that sometimes the person who doesn't know what they're doing walks into the right room and everything clicks.
